label: Teltonika OTD140
description: Outdoor 4G Cat 4 router: 2x 100 Mbps ETH ports, PoE in on one and PoE out on the other.
notes: Vendor figures from the OTD140 datasheet: **2x ETH ports (can be configured as WAN), 10/100 Mbps**, and the power rows read **PoE ports 1 x PoE In**, **PoE standards 802.3af/at**, with a PoE out section on the second port. So the box can be powered by the cable it also passes power through - and **both copper ports are fast Ethernet**, which is the smallest number in an outdoor cellular deployment that otherwise looks modern.

label: Teltonika OXA EBG140
description: Embedded IoT gateway: 1x 1 GbE port, LTE Cat 4.
notes: Vendor figures from the EBG140 (OXA) datasheet: **1 x ETH port, 10/100/1000 Mbps** and an LTE Cat 4 modem. **A single gigabit port** - this is an embedded gateway meant to be built into someone else's enclosure, so its Ethernet is a connection, not a switch.

label: Teltonika RUT276 (RedCap 5G)
description: Compact 5G RedCap router: 1x 100 Mbps WAN, 1x 100 Mbps LAN, PoE in and out.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUT276 datasheet: **1x WAN port 10/100 Mbps** and **1x LAN port, 10/100 Mbps**, with a 5G RedCap modem and PoE on the LAN side. Two ports, both fast Ethernet - the compact RedCap line trades copper speed for size, and the PoE output is what makes a second port unnecessary.

label: Teltonika RUT360
description: Industrial 4G Cat 6 router: 1x 100 Mbps WAN, 1x 100 Mbps LAN, Wi-Fi.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUT360 datasheet: **2 x 10/100 Mbps Ethernet ports** (one WAN, one LAN) with an LTE Cat 6 modem and Wi-Fi. **Cat 6 cellular behind fast Ethernet** - the radio can outrun the ports, so on a good cell the LAN side is the limit.

label: Teltonika RUT951 PoE+
description: Industrial PoE+ router: 1x 100 Mbps WAN (PSE out), 3x 100 Mbps LAN, one PD in and two PSE out, 90 W budget.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUT951 PoE+ datasheet: **1x WAN port 10/100 Mbps** and **3x LAN ports, 10/100 Mbps**. Power: **LAN1 is an 802.3af/at PD input**, **LAN2, LAN3 and WAN are 802.3af/at PSE outputs**, **30 W max per port** and a **90 W budget**. Two things stand out - the **WAN port can source power**, which is unusual, and the whole power budget sits behind four fast-Ethernet ports.

label: Teltonika TCR100 (discontinued)
description: 4G Cat 6 home router, discontinued: 1x 100 Mbps WAN, 1x 100 Mbps LAN, Wi-Fi.
notes: Vendor figures from the TCR100 datasheet: **1 x WAN port 10/100 Mbps** with a LAN port and Wi-Fi, LTE Cat 6. Recorded because units are still in service and still turn up in second-hand stock, **not because it is current** - Teltonika has discontinued it, so treat replacement parts as the real constraint.
